paras: The Mouse Tail Landing shooting was the killing of J. Stafford by a man named Ward at Mouse Tail Landing, on the Tennessee River near Paducah, Kentucky, on Saturday, April 21, 1888, after which "a band of lynchers" was reported to be hunting Ward. Ward escaped from the crowd at the landing, and a Louisville dispatch added an unconfirmed rumor that he had been found and shot to death. The dispatch ran in papers from Washington to California, and several Kansas weeklies headlined it as a killing "With a Rumored Lynching."

According to the Louisville dispatch, Ward was alleged to have been circulating "disrespectful stories" about Stafford's daughter; most other printings read "disreputable stories." Stafford found Ward in a crowd at the landing and, at pistol point, compelled him to confess that he had lied. The dispatch said Stafford "was about to kill him anyhow" but let Ward go after he begged for his life on his knees. The Maysville Evening Bulletin, in a shorter version, said Stafford made "young Ward" kneel and retract "the infamous stories."

Ward went home, came back with a shotgun just as Stafford was mounting his horse, and shot him dead "without a word of warning," according to the wire account. The Evening Bulletin said instead that Stafford was shot as he "turned away." Holding the crowd at bay with the second barrel of his gun, Ward backed off and escaped.

The dispatch then reported that a band of lynchers was searching for him, and the Evening Bulletin wrote that "Lynching parties" were after his "scalp." The fullest version closed with the rumor that Ward "was found yesterday and shot to death," giving no source and no detail.

The coverage does not show whether Ward was caught or killed, since printings as late as May 4 only repeated the dispatch or cut it to a single line. No report of an arrest, an inquest into Stafford's death, or proceedings against Ward or the men hunting him appears in the coverage.

Every account traces to a single Louisville telegram dated April 22, which the Omaha Daily Bee printed as a "Special Telegram" under the headline "He Had His Revenge." Other headlines judged Ward rather than the lynchers: the St. Paul Daily Globe ran "Shot Down by a Coward," the Indianapolis Journal "Slain Without Warning," and the Washington Evening Star "Slandered the Daughter and Killed the Father." The Omaha Bee stated the lynchers' search as fact and left out the rumor of Ward's death.

Kansas weeklies took a version dated April 23 under the heading "Murder at Mousetail Landing," with a deck reading "A Killing on the Tennessee River With a Rumored Lynching." That version named the dead man "John Stafford," and the Nicodemus Cyclone dropped its closing sentences about the lynchers and the rumor. Other papers cut the story to the shooting alone: the Sacramento Daily Record-Union ended with Ward killing Stafford, and the Springfield Daily Republic and the Hickman Courier ran one line saying Stafford "was shot and killed by a man named Ward." None of the reports gave the race of either man, and none commented on the hunt for Ward.

Accounts differed on the moment of the shooting, which the wire placed as Stafford mounted his horse and the Maysville paper as he turned away. Ward's fate also stayed uncertain, because the rumor of his death appeared in some printings and not in others, and all of them rested on the one Louisville dispatch.

reader.title: Mouse Tail Landing shooting
bases: After Ward shot Stafford dead, 'a band of lynchers' was reported hunting him, with an unconfirmed rumor that he was found and shot (A1, A2, A5); no lynching is reported as carried out.

The only report that Ward was killed is a one-sentence rumor that he 'was found yesterday and shot to death', which some printings dropped (A1, A2); the 'band of lynchers' and 'Lynching parties' imply an extralegal group pursuing him for killing Stafford, but no size is given and no killing is confirmed (A1, A5).
Every article traces to one Louisville dispatch of April 22-23 or condenses it (A1, A2, A8, A13); the Maysville paragraph is a rewrite with small differences, not an independent local report (A5).
